identity.name: R^2-gravity scalar-mode dark matter
identity.short_description: A scalar degree of freedom introduced by an R^2 correction to the Einstein-Hilbert action, whose coherent oscillations behave as cold dark matter and whose couplings to the Standard Model are Planck-suppressed.
identity.historical_origin_or_motivation: The paper proposes UV-motivated gravitational degrees of freedom as non-baryonic dark matter, illustrated by the minimal ghost-free R^2 correction.

interactions.flavor_structure: couplings proportional to masses via the energy-momentum trace

theory.notes: The text writes an action with a cosmological term, Einstein-Hilbert term, and an R^2 term with scalar mass parameter m0, while noting higher-energy corrections are needed for UV completion.

symmetries.stabilizing_mechanism: No exact stabilizing symmetry is given; the scalar can be sufficiently long-lived because its Standard Model couplings are Planck-suppressed and decay channels depend on m0.

mechanisms: misalignment mechanism
possible thermal production at UV-sensitive temperatures
production.notes: The paper emphasizes the computable source is coherent misalignment oscillations; thermal production would require the unknown UV completion.

key_dependencies: entropy increase since onset of oscillations

nonstandard_features: UV completion may affect very-high-temperature thermal production

phase_space.notes: The text explicitly compares the abundance mechanism to axion misalignment.

core.range: m0 > 2.7e-3 eV from fifth-force tests; upper limits depend on abundance and decays

core.name: initial scalar displacement
core.description: Initial field value for the misalignment abundance.
core.range: around 1e12 eV can produce non-baryonic DM abundance for suitable parameters

core.name: reduced Planck mass
core.description: Planck-suppressed coupling scale quoted in the action.

validity_domain.condition: The canonical scalar-mode treatment is used in the limit R << m0^2.
Torsion-balance non-observation of a Yukawa force requires m0 > 2.7e-3 eV at 95 percent confidence.
The abundance formula assumes radiation domination at the onset of oscillations and adiabatic scaling with entropy.

global.description: The R^2 term is used as the minimal ghost-free illustration of high-energy gravitational corrections.
Matter is assumed to be minimally coupled to gravity in the Jordan frame, producing the trace coupling.
The initial scalar value need not be at the potential minimum when H exceeds m0.

robustness.notes: The core model is well specified in the assigned text, while viability is parameter-dependent.

warnings.warning: The scalar mode is not exactly stable; viability depends on lifetime and mass-dependent decay channels.
